title: When Hate Meets Facts: LLMs-in-the-Loop for Check-worthiness Detection in Hate Speech
measurement_description: The paper primarily measures the ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to detect check-worthy claims within hate speech messages (differentiating between Non-Factual, Unimportant Factual, and Check-worthy Factual statements). While the main focus is not religion, an auxiliary analysis evaluates the check-worthiness of hate speech targeting specific demographic groups, including religious groups (Jews and Muslims) using the MT-CONAN dataset.
findings: In its evaluation of hate speech disaggregated by target groups (Table D), the paper found significant variations in how check-worthy claims are distributed. When applying the Olmo2-32B model to the MT-CONAN dataset, it found that 65.15% of hate speech messages targeting Jews contained Check-worthy Factual Statements (CFS), whereas 46.44% of messages targeting Muslims contained CFS. Conversely, a higher percentage of hate speech directed at Muslims relied on Non-Factual Statements (52.06%) compared to hate speech directed at Jews (32.49%).
